name: Gearbox
text: Adopt **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** for EXCAVA’s heavy lifting. It’s a single-model solution with strong reasoning, lower latency than mixtral-8x22B, and proven performance on complex tasks—no ensemble overhead. Trade-off: it’s not the absolute top performer, but the gap to the best isn’t worth the added cost and complexity.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct trades raw power for stability—fine if we’re stuck in a compute crunch, but EXCAVA’s ceiling is capped by its reasoning ceiling. The real risk: we hit a wall where even 0.5% gains require top-tier models, not just stable ones. Test Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct against the latest Anthropic or Mistral heavyweights on a controlled benchmark—if it lags by more than 1% on complex tasks, we pivot to a multi-model ensemble or a newer single model like Llama 4.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** for EXCAVA’s core reasoning tasks. It delivers 90% of the performance of top-tier models like Anthropic’s latest at half the cost and latency, with no ensemble bloat—directly lifting EXCAVA’s capability without hitting compute walls. Trade-off: we cap peak performance at ~0.5% gains, but that’s enough to outpace incremental improvements from unstable bleeding-edge models.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s stability won’t bridge EXCAVA’s ceiling—if the latest Anthropic model (Claude Mythos 5) delivers even a 0.5% reasoning edge, the gap compounds under load. Test the two head-to-head on EXCAVA’s hardest tasks; if Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct loses by >0.5%, the risk isn’t compute—it’s leaving capability on the table.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a controlled A/B test between Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Claude Mythos 5 on EXCAVA’s hardest tasks—if Mythos 5 wins by >0.5%, adopt it; else, keep Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. Result: clear winner with proof delivered by Gearbox. Owner: Torque.
